Subject: Re: Draft order form redlines — a couple items on term/termination

Hi Alicia — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Markus (finance) to propose concrete options.

High-level response:
- Auto-renew notice: we can accommodate 60 days with a small commercial trade-off (see options below). 90 days is possible but would likely require a term-adjusted pricing concession.
- Termination for convenience: our standard is prorated refunds for unused prepaid credits; early-exit fees are uncommon except where reserved capacity or committed GPU pools are involved. For pilots or seats we usually do prorate + 30 day decommission assistance.

Karthik/Markus — can you propose 2-3 clean language alternatives for the MSA/order form: 
A) 60-day notice, no exit fee, prorated refund of prepayments;
B) 60-day notice, modest exit fee (e.g., 10% of remaining committed ARR) if Reserved/Dedicated capacity was provisioned;
C) 90-day notice with no exit fee but a small onboarding fee credit to cover reserved capacity prep.

Alicia — once we align language we can produce a tracked redline and a short offboarding runbook (ops checklist) that lays out data export, KV cache eviction schedule, and transfer of billing.

Quick ask: whats your target signature date? That helps us pick the least disruptive option.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft order form redlines — a couple items on term/termination

Eve / Markus — quick legal perspective and suggested block language. Quoting Alicia below where relevant.

On auto-renew and notice window: the cleanest is to keep the MSA auto-renew clause but allow the order form to set an alternative notice window. Suggested text (Option A — simplest):
"Either party may elect not to renew an Order Form by providing at least sixty (60) days prior written notice to the other party prior to the then-current Term expiration date. Absent timely notice, the Order Form will automatically renew for an additional term equal to the expiring Term under the same pricing and service levels."

On Termination for Convenience: recommended default = prorated refund of prepaid, plus a 30-day operational wind-down period during which Redwood will provide reasonable assistance to export data and transfer access. For Reserved/Dedicated setups where capacity was provisioned in advance, propose an additional limited exit charge tied to irrecoverable provisioning costs. Suggested clause (Option B):
"Customer may terminate an Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days prior written notice. If termination occurs after Redwood has provisioned Dedicated capacity specifically for Customer, Customer shall pay a one-time termination charge equal to ten percent (10%) of the remaining fees due under the Order Form to cover costs of provisioning. All prepayments for unused service will be refunded on a prorated basis. Redwood will provide up to thirty (30) days of transition support at no additional charge."

Operational notes:
- Need to clarify what counts as "provisioned" (committed GPU pool vs. seat license).
- Recommend a definition in the order form for "Dedicated Capacity" and a schedule for deprovisioning so procurement can assess cost exposure.

Markus — confirm if 10% is acceptable commercially or if finance prefers a flat minimum fee (e.g., $25k) for high-TCV deals.

I can produce a tracked redline for the MSA and a short offboarding runbook.

-Karthik
General Counsel (acting)
Redwood Inference

- ToC: prefer prorated refund (no exit fee) for standard hosted usage. We understand the dedicated capacity carveout; our procurement team will accept a provisioning-related exit charge but would like a lens: either 10% of remaining fees OR documented provisioning costs (whichever is lower).
- Deprovisioning: request a 45-day transition assistance window (to cover data export and validation).

Were targeting a 2026-02-15 signature date (tight end of our internal timeline). If you can turn a redline by end-of-week, procurement will review and well route to legal.

Attached: weve highlighted the order form quantities we plan to sign once the termination language is finalized.

Next steps we propose from our side: you produce the tracked changes for the MSA and an offboarding checklist.

Best,
Alicia
